content: I’ll first read the workspace contract and rollout evidence, then use the required fish-control shelf and the wake-visual inspection skill before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’m using `fish-control-primitives` because the protocol explicitly requires it, and `read-wake-visual-signals-first` because this is a multi-wake policy change whose visual evidence must shape the controller.

The required skills confirm the order: anchor images to observations and metrics, inspect the shared prewarm and rollout sheets, then consult the primitive references. I’m now inventorying the inherited evidence and candidate without changing anything.

The visual and diagnostic evidence shows the inherited bearing-history mechanism did produce a semantic improvement—capture improved from `43.9505` to `41.503`—but at a clear load cost (`61.80/862.48` vs `49.44/701.26` force/moment). The route remains one decisive redirect followed by direct upstream swimming; no sampled failure sheet exists, so the inherited lower-boundary seed failure is the available failure boundary. With that evidence anchored, I’m consulting the bookshelf for one mechanism that can address the arrival/load tradeoff without reopening the rejected gain, phase, amplitude, or range axes.

The shelf’s useful invariant here is a complementary separation of roles: slow body-frame target history determines route, while a minimal actuator-side projection limits only cap-driving outward acceleration after alignment and leaves reversal/thrust commands intact. This is supported by two independent sampled results: history filtering improved arrival by `2.448` time units, and the evaluated two-joint projection reduced command energy and RMS loads without delaying the unfiltered carrier. I’ll record that falsifiable combination in the candidate notes before touching the policy, as required by the visual-first skill.

The single candidate now combines the two measured mechanisms, and the durable guidance records the newly evaluated history tradeoff without claiming this unevaluated combination as evidence. I’m moving into boundary/schema checks and the mandated workspace checker; no CFD will be run.

The mandated guidance check exposed a workspace metadata issue before assessing my edits: `README.md` contains the same assigned parent marker twice, so the checker reports two parents. I’m inspecting the checker and the duplicated lines to make the smallest in-workspace repair consistent with the “rerun until pass” requirement; the candidate and guidance themselves remain intact.

The required checker is now partly complete: guidance and boundary checks pass. The prescribed Julia contract check cannot start because this workspace has no `julia` executable, matching the inherited environment limitation. I’m compensating with static schema/boundary analysis and a broad algebraic state sweep of the exact policy equations, then I’ll record that verification result in the notes.
